title: Managing Critical State: Distributed Consensus for Reliability
provenance_note: Rendered to PDF from the official HTML chapter; the published full-book PDF no longer resolves (the static.googleusercontent.com target returns 404). The PDF contains the chapter body text only, without figures or tables. Chapter edited by Tim Harvey.
abstract: Processes crash or may need to be restarted. Hard drives fail. Natural disasters can take out several datacenters in a region. Site Reliability Engineers need to anticipate these sorts of failures and develop strategies to keep systems running in spite of them. These strategies usually entail running such systems across multiple sites. Geographically distributing a system is relatively straightforward, but also introduces the need to maintain a consistent view of system state, which is a more nuanced and difficult undertaking.
